answer: One licensed observatory post gives each applicant a telescope for 120 days, with a 150 token deposit frozen and a 90 dollar license. The keeper logs each nebula seen at the zenith with a photo, and a neighbor signs the tally weekly. A shelter serves as a haven for the logbook, sealed nightly with a numbered tag. Forging it forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper 180 days, so faking 10,000 posts freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 900,000 dollars. Like a shepherd counting sheep through his own gate, the post credits only nights it watched, and a faker ends up guarding an empty ridge.
